name: Food Prices and Affordability
justification: Prices decide how much food a given income buys (economic access); price swings are a stability concern.

name: Local Food Production and Supply
justification: Local output is physical availability; production shocks are instability; farm and fisher income is access for producer households.

name: Climate and Weather Hazards
justification: Hazards are the main source of instability in supply and livelihoods; they reduce availability through production.

name: Household Income and Employment
justification: Income and remittances are economic access; job losses and remittance drops are income shocks (stability).

name: Structural Poverty and Vulnerability
justification: Poverty and food poverty limit access; a high food budget share and subsistence poverty point to diets at risk (utilization, indirect only).

name: Food Stress News Signals
justification: News reports are an early, cross-cutting warning of instability; they do not measure a dimension directly.

name: Experienced Hunger
justification: Experienced hunger measures inadequate access and, through insufficient intake, utilization; its persistence reflects stability. Direct utilization data (OPT Plus, NDHS) are not available at province-quarter level: a disclosed gap.
